get_organization.title: Get the organization
get_organization.description: The organization this Admin key belongs to -- its id and name. The cheapest call that proves the credential is a working admin credential, and the source of the organization id the federation and analytics surfaces want.

list_users.title: List organization members
list_users.description: Page through the organization's members with their emails and roles. Filterable by exact email or by role. Roles run user, claude_code_user, developer, billing, admin -- plus owner and primary owner, which the API reports but cannot assign.

after_id.description: Return the page immediately after this user id.

before_id.description: Return the page immediately before this user id.

email.description: Return only the member with this exact email address.

roles.description: Filter to one or more organization roles.

get_user.title: Get an organization member
get_user.description: One member by id, with their email, name, organization role and when they were added. Use it to confirm who a user id refers to before changing or removing them.

update_user.title: Change a member's role
update_user.description: Set a member's organization role. This is a POST to the member's own path, not a PATCH. Raising someone to `admin` grants them the ability to manage every other member, so treat it as a privileged change.

output.description: The member with their new role.

remove_user.title: Remove a member from the organization
remove_user.description: Remove someone from the organization entirely. They lose access to every workspace at once, and re-adding them means a fresh invite -- there is no undo and no soft-delete for members.

output.description: Confirmation that the member was removed.

create_invite.title: Invite someone to the organization
create_invite.description: Send an invitation with the role the person will hold once they accept, and optionally the RBAC groups they should join. The invite is pending until accepted -- creating one does not make them a member or consume a seat yet.

role.description: The organization role the invitee will hold.

rbac_group_ids.description: RBAC groups to add the person to when they accept.

output.description: The created invite and its status.

list_invites.title: List invites
list_invites.description: Page through the organization's invitations, filterable by email, role or status. The way to see who has been invited but has not accepted, and to find the invite id needed to revoke one.

after_id.description: Return the page immediately after this invite id.

before_id.description: Return the page immediately before this invite id.

email.description: Return only invites to this exact address.

roles.description: Filter by the role the invite grants.

statuses.description: Filter by invite status, e.g. pending, accepted or expired.

get_invite.title: Get an invite
get_invite.description: One invitation by id, with the address it went to, the role it grants and its current status. Useful for checking whether an invite is still pending before re-sending one.

delete_invite.title: Revoke an invite
delete_invite.description: Cancel a pending invitation so the link stops working. Harmless on an invite the person has not accepted; it does not remove someone who already joined -- use remove_user for that.

output.description: Confirmation that the invite was revoked.

list_rbac_groups.title: List RBAC groups
list_rbac_groups.description: Page through the organization's role-based access control groups. Groups are how permissions are granted to sets of people rather than one at a time, and their ids are what create_invite's rbac_group_ids takes.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

get_rbac_group.title: Get an RBAC group
get_rbac_group.description: One RBAC group by id, with its name. Use it to confirm which group an id refers to before adding people to it or deleting it.

create_rbac_group.title: Create an RBAC group
create_rbac_group.description: Create a new role-based access control group by name. The group starts empty -- add people with add_rbac_group_member, or name it on an invite so they join on acceptance.

update_rbac_group.title: Rename an RBAC group
update_rbac_group.description: Change an RBAC group's name. A POST to the group's own path, like every other update in this API. Membership and permissions are unaffected.

delete_rbac_group.title: Delete an RBAC group
delete_rbac_group.description: Delete an RBAC group. Its members stay in the organization but lose whatever access the group granted them, which can silently break someone mid-task -- check the membership first.

group_id.description: The RBAC group id to delete.

output.description: Confirmation that the group was deleted.

list_rbac_group_members.title: List an RBAC group's members
list_rbac_group_members.description: Page through the people in one RBAC group. Read this before deleting a group or revoking its permissions, since it is the only place the blast radius of that change is visible.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

output.description: A page of the group's members.

add_rbac_group_member.title: Add a member to an RBAC group
add_rbac_group_member.description: Put an existing organization member into an RBAC group, granting them whatever that group carries. The person must already be a member of the organization; this does not invite them.

remove_rbac_group_member.title: Remove a member from an RBAC group
remove_rbac_group_member.description: Take someone out of an RBAC group. They keep their organization membership and any access granted elsewhere, but lose what this group conferred.

user_id.description: The user id to remove from the group.

output.description: Confirmation that the membership was removed.

list_rbac_roles.title: List RBAC roles
list_rbac_roles.description: The role definitions available in the organization, including any custom ones. Read-only -- roles are defined in the Console, not created through this API.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

get_rbac_role.title: Get an RBAC role
get_rbac_role.description: One role definition by id. Pair it with list_rbac_role_permissions to see exactly what the role allows before assigning it to anyone.

list_rbac_role_permissions.title: List an RBAC role's permissions
list_rbac_role_permissions.description: Every permission one role grants. This is the audit answer to "what can someone with this role actually do", which the role's name alone does not settle.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

output.description: A page of the role's permissions.

create_workspace.title: Create a workspace
create_workspace.description: Create a workspace -- the unit API keys, rate limits and spend are scoped to. `data_residency` pins where inference runs and `external_key_id` attaches a customer-managed encryption key; both are easier to set here than to change later.

data_residency.description: Where inference for this workspace should run.

display_color.description: The colour the Console shows for the workspace.

external_key_id.description: A registered CMEK external key to encrypt the workspace with.

tags.description: Tags to attach to the workspace.

list_workspaces.title: List workspaces
list_workspaces.description: Page through the organization's workspaces. Archived ones are hidden unless `include_archived` is set -- which is why a workspace that still exists can appear missing from this list.

after_id.description: Return the page immediately after this workspace id.

before_id.description: Return the page immediately before this workspace id.

include_archived.description: Include archived workspaces, which are otherwise omitted.

get_workspace.title: Get a workspace
get_workspace.description: One workspace by id, with its name, display colour, data residency and archive state. The source of the workspace id every workspace-scoped tool below takes.

update_workspace.title: Update a workspace
update_workspace.description: Change a workspace's name, colour, tags, data residency or attached CMEK key. Attaching an external key is done here rather than through a dedicated endpoint. A POST, not a PATCH.

name.description: A new name for the workspace.

data_residency.description: Where inference for this workspace should run.

display_color.description: The colour the Console shows for the workspace.

external_key_id.description: A registered CMEK external key to attach to the workspace.

archive_workspace.title: Archive a workspace
archive_workspace.description: Archive a workspace, which stops it being used while leaving it visible to list_workspaces under `include_archived`. Its API keys stop working, so this is disruptive even though nothing is deleted.

add_workspace_member.title: Add a member to a workspace
add_workspace_member.description: Give an existing organization member access to one workspace, at a workspace role -- workspace_user, workspace_developer, workspace_admin or workspace_billing. Organization admins already reach every workspace and do not need adding.

workspace_role.description: The role they hold in this workspace.

list_workspace_members.title: List a workspace's members
list_workspace_members.description: Page through who has access to one workspace and at what role. Note that organization admins have access without appearing here, so this is not the complete list of people who can reach the workspace.

after_id.description: Return the page immediately after this user id.

before_id.description: Return the page immediately before this user id.

get_workspace_member.title: Get a workspace member
get_workspace_member.description: One person's membership of one workspace, with the role they hold there. Cheaper than paging the whole roster when you already know the user id.

update_workspace_member.title: Change a workspace member's role
update_workspace_member.description: Set the role someone holds in one workspace. Their organization role is untouched -- these are separate ladders, and a workspace_admin is not an organization admin.

remove_workspace_member.title: Remove a member from a workspace
remove_workspace_member.description: Revoke one person's access to one workspace. They stay in the organization and keep access to any other workspace they belong to.

user_id.description: The user id to remove from the workspace.

output.description: Confirmation that the membership was removed.

add_workspace_service_account.title: Add a service account to a workspace
add_workspace_service_account.description: Give a service account access to one workspace at a workspace role. This is how an automated workload gets scoped credentials without a human member behind them. Unlike the organization-level service-account endpoints, this one works with an Admin API key.

workspace_role.description: The role the service account holds in this workspace.

list_workspace_service_accounts.title: List a workspace's service accounts
list_workspace_service_accounts.description: Page through the service accounts with access to one workspace. The audit view of which automated workloads can spend against it, which the human member list does not show.

limit.description: How many service accounts per page.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

output.description: A page of workspace service accounts.

get_workspace_service_account.title: Get a workspace's service account membership
get_workspace_service_account.description: One service account's membership of one workspace, with the role it holds. Use it to confirm an automated workload's access level before changing or revoking it.

update_workspace_service_account.title: Change a service account's workspace role
update_workspace_service_account.description: Set the role a service account holds in one workspace. Lowering it can break a running workload immediately, since its existing keys start failing rather than degrading.

remove_workspace_service_account.title: Remove a service account from a workspace
remove_workspace_service_account.description: Revoke a service account's access to one workspace. Any workload authenticating through it against that workspace stops working immediately, so check what depends on it first.

service_account_id.description: The service account id to remove.

output.description: Confirmation that the membership was removed.

list_api_keys.title: List API keys
list_api_keys.description: Page through the organization's API keys with their names, status, workspace and creator. Key *values* are never returned -- only metadata. The key ids here are what the usage report's api_key_ids filter takes.

after_id.description: Return the page immediately after this key id.

before_id.description: Return the page immediately before this key id.

workspace_id.description: Only keys scoped to this workspace.

created_by_user_id.description: Only keys created by this member.

output.description: A page of API key records, without the key values.

get_api_key.title: Get an API key
get_api_key.description: One API key's metadata -- name, status, workspace and who created it. The secret itself is never retrievable after creation, so this cannot recover a lost key.

update_api_key.title: Rename or deactivate an API key
update_api_key.description: Change an API key's name or status. Setting status to `inactive` is the immediate kill switch for a leaked key -- every request using it starts failing at once, and there is no grace period.

name.description: A new name for the key.

status.description: The key's new status. `inactive` disables it immediately.

list_rate_limits.title: List the organization's rate limits
list_rate_limits.description: The configured rate limits for the organization, optionally narrowed to one model or limit group. These are the *configured* ceilings, not current consumption -- for what is actually being used, read the usage report.

model.description: Only limits for this model, e.g. "claude-opus-5".

group_type.description: Only limits of this group type.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

output.description: A page of configured rate limits.

list_workspace_rate_limits.title: List a workspace's rate limits
list_workspace_rate_limits.description: The rate limits configured for one workspace. Where an organization splits capacity across workspaces, this is what says how much each is allowed, and therefore why one workspace is throttling while another is not.

group_type.description: Only limits of this group type.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

output.description: A page of the workspace's rate limits.

get_usage_report.title: Get the token usage report
get_usage_report.description: Token consumption over a time range, bucketed by minute, hour or day and optionally grouped by model, workspace, API key, service tier, inference geo or speed. This is the accurate source for usage -- more reliable than summing `usage` off responses. Bucket counts are capped per granularity (1440 at 1m, 168 at 1h, 31 at 1d), so long ranges need several calls.

starting_at.description: Start of the range, ISO 8601 UTC, e.g. "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z".

ending_at.description: End of the range, ISO 8601 UTC.

group_by.description: Dimensions to break the numbers down by, e.g. model, workspace_id, api_key_id, service_tier, inference_geo.

workspace_ids.description: Only these workspaces. The default workspace reports as null.

api_key_ids.description: Only these API keys. Console playground usage has no key and reports as null.

service_tiers.description: Only these service tiers, e.g. batch or priority.

context_window.description: Only these context window buckets, e.g. "0-200k".

inference_geos.description: Only these inference geographies -- global, us or not_available.

page.description: The `next_page` cursor from the previous response.

output.description: Token usage per bucket, broken down by the requested dimensions.

get_cost_report.title: Get the cost report
get_cost_report.description: Costs in USD over a range, daily granularity only, groupable by workspace or description. Amounts are decimal strings in cents. Two gaps worth knowing: Priority Tier costs are not included here at all, and code execution shows up here but not in the usage report.

starting_at.description: Start of the range, ISO 8601 UTC.

ending_at.description: End of the range, ISO 8601 UTC.

group_by.description: Dimensions to break costs down by -- workspace_id and description.

page.description: The `next_page` cursor from the previous response.

output.description: Daily costs in cents, broken down by the requested dimensions.

get_claude_code_analytics.title: Get Claude Code analytics
get_claude_code_analytics.description: Per-user Claude Code metrics for a single UTC day -- sessions, lines added and removed, commits, pull requests, per-tool accept/reject counts and estimated cost by model. `starting_at` is a date, not a timestamp, and names one day only; there is no range. Data lags real time by up to an hour.

starting_at.description: The UTC day to report on, as YYYY-MM-DD. One day per call.

page.description: The `next_page` cursor from the previous response.

output.description: One record per user for that day, with productivity metrics and estimated cost.

list_service_accounts.title: List service accounts
list_service_accounts.description: The organization's service accounts. This endpoint rejects an Admin API key -- it needs an `org:admin` OAuth bearer token, so on a key-only connection it answers 401 rather than an empty list.

limit.description: How many service accounts per page.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

create_service_account.title: Create a service account
create_service_account.description: Create a service account for an automated workload, at an organization role. Needs an `org:admin` OAuth bearer token rather than an Admin API key. Pair it with a workspace membership to scope what it can spend against.

name.description: A name for the service account.

organization_role.description: The organization role the service account holds.

archive_service_account.title: Archive a service account
archive_service_account.description: Archive a service account so it can no longer authenticate. Any workload using it stops immediately. Needs an `org:admin` OAuth bearer token rather than an Admin API key.

service_account_id.description: The service account id to archive.

list_federation_issuers.title: List workload identity federation issuers
list_federation_issuers.description: The OIDC issuers trusted for workload identity federation, such as GitHub Actions. Needs an `org:admin` OAuth bearer token rather than an Admin API key.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

list_federation_rules.title: List workload identity federation rules
list_federation_rules.description: The rules mapping an external identity's claims onto a service account and OAuth scope -- how CI exchanges its own JWT for Anthropic credentials. Needs an `org:admin` OAuth bearer token rather than an Admin API key.

page.description: Page cursor from the previous response.

create_external_key.title: Register a CMEK external key
create_external_key.description: Register a customer-managed encryption key held in your own KMS. Registering is only the first step -- validate it, then attach it to a workspace with update_workspace's external_key_id before it protects anything.

display_name.description: A name for the key in the Console.

geo.description: The geography the key applies in, e.g. "us".

validate_external_key.title: Validate a CMEK external key
validate_external_key.description: Check that Anthropic can actually reach and use a registered key. Run this before attaching the key to a workspace -- a key that fails validation will not encrypt anything, and the failure is easier to diagnose here than on a workspace update.

output.description: The validation result for the key.
